subject: computer-science
title: Divide and Conquer
welcome_lead: Break a problem in two, solve, combine — repeat.
meta_desc: A-Level CS: divide-and-conquer, merge sort, quicksort and recurrences.
final_note: Divide-and-conquer powers many of the fastest algorithms.

concepts.def: Solve by dividing, conquering subproblems, then combining.
Sort by halving, sorting each half, then merging — O(n log n).

walkthroughs.body_html: Divide the problem into smaller subproblems, conquer each recursively, then combine the answers. Sorting, FFT, closest pair and many more follow this pattern.
Merge sort: split the array in half, sort each, merge sorted halves. The recurrence T(n) = 2T(n/2) + n solves to O(n log n) in all cases.
Quicksort picks a pivot, partitions smaller/larger, and recurses. Average O(n log n); worst O(n^2) on bad pivots (sorted input with a fixed pivot). Randomising the pivot avoids the worst case.
